Indian Standard ROASTED GROUND COFFEE -- DETERMINATION OF MOISTURE CONTENT -- KARL FISCHER METHOD (REFERENCE METHOD)

� BIS 2012

BUREAU OF INDIAN STANDARDS
MANAK BHAVAN, 9 BAHADUR SHAH ZAFAR MARG NEW DELHI 110002 December 2012 Price Group 3

Stimulant Foods Sectional Committee, FAD 6

NATIONAL FOREWORD This Indian Standard which is identical with ISO 11817 : 1994 `Roasted ground coffee -- Determination of moisture content -- Karl Fischer method (Reference method)' issued by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on the recommendation of the Stimulant Foods Sectional Committee and approval of the Food and Agriculture Division Council. The text of ISO Standard has been approved as suitable for publication as an Indian Standard without deviations. Certain conventions are, however, not identical to those used in Indian Standards. Attention is particularly drawn to the following: a) Wherever the words `International Standard' appear referring to this standard, they should be read as `Indian Standard'. b) Comma (,) has been used as a decimal marker while in Indian Standards, the current practice is to use a point (.) as the decimal marker. In this adopted standard, reference appear to the following International Standard for which Indian Standard also exists. The corresponding Indian Standard which is to be substituted in its place is listed below along with its degree of equivalence for the edition indicated: International Standard Corresponding Indian Standard Degree of Equivalence Technically Equivalent

ISO 760 : 1978 Determination of IS 2362 : 1993 Determination of water -- Karl Fischer method water by Karl Fischer method -- Test (General method) method

In reporting the result of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'.

10.4

Determination

of blank value

10.1 Determination Fischer reagent

of titre of the Karl

Pipette 50,O ml of the dried methanol into a dried 100 ml round-bottomed flask (7.3.2) and boil with running cooling water for 30 min. Then allow the round-bottomed flask to cool, remove it from the apparatus and close the flask immediately. Take an aliquot par-t of IO,0 ml for titration of the blank value and titrate it as described in 10.5 and 10.6. Record the volume of Karl Fischer reagent used.

Determine the titre of the reagent (6.1) in accordance with ISO 760. For an exact dosage of smaller amounts of water, use the Syringe (7.5), the discharge of which is obtained by differente weighing with the ultra-microbalance (7.2.1). Determine the volume required by several titrations (10.6) of 30 mg to 40 mg of water and calculate the titre, T, according to the following formula:

Boil for a fur-ther 30 min at reflux. Then allow the roundbottomed flask to cool to room temperature, remove it from the reflux condenser and close the flask immediately.

10.2

Preparation

of glassware

10.6

Preparation

of the titration

apparatus

Keep all required glassware in the oven (7.1) set at 40 "C. Prior to use, allow the glassware to cool to room temperature in the desiccator (7.6) and store it there.

Prepare the titration apparatus (7.4) in accordance with the manufacturer' s instructions. The air-tightness of the titration vessel is of special importante.
A measure of lack of air-tightness is the leakage NOTE 3 rate ( pg H,O per min) of the System. This tan be between IO pg/min and 60 pg/min depending on the ambient air humidity. The determination of the leakage rate is made in accordance with the instructions of the manufacturer of the Karl Fischer titrator used and should not exceed 60 pg/min for the determination.

10.3

Preparation

of reflux apparatus

Place 75 ml of methanol (6.2) in a 100 ml roundbottomed flask (7.3.2). Adjust the heating rate of the heating device (7.3.1), with the cooling water supply closed, by means of the thyristor regulator so that the methanol condenses at the upper end of the reflux condenser (7.3.3). Note the adjustment. Then close the apparatus with the drying tube (7.3.4) and boil the methanol at an unchanged heating rate for 30 min under reflux. Open the cooling water supply and allow the apparatus to cool. DO not remove the flask until the apparatus has cooled to room temperature. After this preparation, remove any adhering water from the inner surface of the reflux condenser. Immediately after having removed the flasks, close the reflux apparatus thus prepared with a round-bottomed flask containing an effective drying agent (molecular sieve or silica gel with humidity indicator).

titration

Place 35 ml of the dried methanol (receiver) in the vessel. Take care that the metallic Parts of the platinum double electrode (7.4.2) are immersed completely. Before the first daily use, condition the System in a so-called stand-by titration for 20 min when the adhered water is removed completely.

10.7

Determination

Depending on the expected water content of the roasted ground coffee samples, take an aliquot part of IO,0 ml [water content < 3 % (dm)] or 5,0 ml from the Sample [water content > 3 % (dm)] extracted in accordance with 10.5 and pipette it rap-

The dosage of the reagent and the recognition of the end-point is controlled automatically by the apparatus. Adjust the apparatus so that the electronie titration ends if no potential Change of more than 15 mV ocCUTSwithin 20 s. Carry out three titrations on each extract (or for determination of the blank value). DO not Change receiver (see 10.6). 11.2

Precision

Results of an interlaboratory test are given in annex A. The interlaboratory test was carried out using vacuum-packed samples exclusively. 11.2.1 Repeatability

11 11 .l

Expression
Calculation

of results

The absolute differente between two independent test results, obtained using the Same method on identical test material in the Same laboratory by the same Operator using the Same equipment within a shot-t interval of time, should not be greater than 0,14 %. 11.2.2 Reproducibility
